title: Power Pages: SDK for native mobile apps and kiosks
summary: Hold: the table-permission automation lists components but cannot change permissions, despite appearing beside a configuration control. The roadmap facts match the record, and targeted searches found no documentation resolving the SDK-specific licensing, default or administrator-switch questions.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first row
claims.claim: Portal Management app > Website > Site settings reaches the site-setting control.
claims.quote: Using the Portal Management app, select Site settings under the Website section. ... To edit an existing setting, select the Site Setting listed in the grid.
claims.fix: Extend the existing-setting route to 'Website > Site settings > site setting' in front matter and the rendered table. The current route reaches the correct list but stops before opening the setting.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first row
claims.claim: POST to /api/data/v9.2/mspp_sitesettings can create the enabled site setting using the printed name, value and website binding.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/mspp_sitesettings; Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE; mspp_name; mspp_value; mspp_websiteid | mspp_website
claims.fix: Set api.call and the rendered call to 'POST [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/mspp_sitesettings', without a body. Add to the note: 'The request body sets mspp_name to Webapi/<table-name>/enabled, mspp_value to true, and mspp_websiteid@odata.bind to the website reference.'

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: first row
claims.claim: Creating only the enabled setting is not a complete portals Web API configuration.
claims.quote: This setting is required unless Webapi/<table-name>/UseFieldsFromView is set to True and the configured system view contains at least one eligible column.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second row
claims.claim: Power Pages design studio > Security > Protect > Table permissions reaches table-permission configuration.
claims.quote: In the design studio from the side menu, select Security. ... in the Protect section, select Table permissions ... Select the table permission that you want to edit
claims.fix: Extend the existing-permission route to 'Security > Protect > Table permissions > table permission' in front matter and the rendered table. The current route reaches the correct list but stops before opening a permission.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second row
claims.claim: GET /api/data/v9.2/powerpagecomponents is the automation alongside the control deciding table-permission records and privileges.
claims.quote: Update operations use the HTTP PATCH verb. Pass a JSON object containing the properties you want to update to the URI that represents the record.
claims.fix: Replace the read-only inventory call with 'PATCH [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/mspp_entitypermissions(<permission-id>)' and set docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/reference/mspp_entitypermission. Replace the inventory/type-18 note with: 'Updates an existing table permission: mspp_scope sets the access type; mspp_read, mspp_write, mspp_create, mspp_delete, mspp_append and mspp_appendto set privileges. Association with a web role is still required.' Retain the SDK applicability caveat and apply the same replacement to the rendered row. The original GET exists and the note correctly calls it read-only, but it does not configure this control.
